title: "Quiz 4 Student Guide"
description: "Paper quiz on R Weeks 10–12: format, preparation and practice."
---

## At A Glance

| Item | Quiz 4 arrangement |
|---|---|
| Delivery | Individual **paper quiz**, with a separate version for each section |
| Timing | **15 minutes** of working time; exact section dates announced in Blackboard |
| Coverage | **R, Weeks 10–12**; earlier R fundamentals are used within these topics |
| Format | **6 single-choice MCQs × 1 mark + 3 short written responses × 2 marks = 12 marks** |
| Balance | Four marks each for Weeks 10, 11 and 12 |
| Preparation | Core exercises and the [separate practice quiz](quiz-04-practice.qmd) |

Quiz 4 retains the working Week 13 place in the course schedule. Both sections
will have completed the assessed teaching before the first sitting. MATLAB
and material first introduced in Week 13 or later are excluded.

## What To Practise

| Week | Focus |
|---|---|
| [10](../weeks/week-10.qmd) | Explain the meaning assumption behind cleaning; distinguish observation and lookup keys; reason about join matches, unmatched rows and preservation; understand what a check establishes and what it does not |
| [11](../weeks/week-11.qmd) | Read short pipelines and explain row meaning at checkpoints; trace a function under a stated contract; choose a revealing test and give its expected result |
| [12](../weeks/week-12.qmd) | Use vector operations without losing positions; distinguish list results from typed scalar results; keep failed requests visible in a complete batch record |

The priority is the **Core** selection on each week's exercise page. Guided
and extension tasks are not automatically additional requirements. You do
not need to write a long program, run R, memorize the classroom dataset or
perform lengthy arithmetic. All data and contracts needed for a question
will be supplied. No calculator is needed.

## How Marks Are Awarded

- MCQs have one best answer: **1 mark** for the correct choice and **0** otherwise.
  No justification is required and there is no negative marking.
- Each written question has **two explicit one-mark parts**. Each part can
  earn 0, 0.5 or 1, so relevant partial reasoning receives credit.
- Answer the requested parts directly. One or two short sentences, bullets,
  or a small input/output example will usually suffice. Length suggestions
  are guides rather than strict limits.
- Equivalent correct wording and methods are accepted. English polish and
  unrequested details do not earn or lose marks.

For example, be able to pair a specific check with the failure it could
detect, or a test input with the expected output under a stated rule. A
successful run, an expected row count or a unique key is useful evidence,
but each has a limited job.

## Practice And Arrangements

Attempt the [ungraded practice quiz](quiz-04-practice.qmd) on paper in
15 minutes before opening its self-check feedback. Its situations differ
from both live versions. Use the feedback to check each part of your reasoning.

Work individually. R execution, AI, websites, messaging and collaboration
are not permitted during the quiz. Follow the permitted-reference instructions
announced in Blackboard; the practice page does not introduce a new reference
sheet or calculator policy. Blackboard also provides section dates and
accommodation arrangements.

The existing [missed-assessment policy](../syllabus/index.qmd#missed-assessments-and-late-project-submissions)
and lowest-quiz-drop rule remain unchanged. Live questions and their keys
remain private.
